newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - FINANCIAL TIMES - AUGUST 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - FINANCIAL TIMES - AUGUST 11.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. For further information on these articles or details of BMC's other international press and broadcast services call Simon McMillan on "44 (0)171 256 5130 or e-mail bmc.co@ft.com -- HAMPEL 'OMISSIONS' ATTACKED

Institutional shareholder groups, company secretaries and lawyers have voiced dissatisfaction alongside the governments' confusion of certain aspects of the Hampel committee report on corporate governance which fund management company Hermes's corporate focus director, Peter Butler, has termed as omissions. Mr Butler voiced several concerns over the report, in particular the vagueness surrounding the definition of an independent non- executive director.
-- CRUNCH MEETING FOR PITCHER AT UNITED

United Utilities executive chairman, Sir Desmond Pitcher, is asking for support from boardroom colleagues over calls from shareholders for his dismissal from the company. A boardroom meeting tomorrow is planned to discuss Sir Desmond's future following the public boardroom row concerning Sir Pitcher's necessity within the company. Sir Peter Middleton, non-executive director with the multi-utility has intensified the debate by canvassing opinion in the city.
-- SHELL OPENS UP IN BID TO BECOME INVESTOR FRIENDLY

Anglo-Dutch oil company Royal Dutch/Shell is for the first time to publicly disclose its performance, in relation to internal targets, alongside plans for the company to cease its policy of not visiting any major shareholder in a bid to become more investor-friendly. Shell Transport and Trading chairman Mark Moody-Stuart announced the intentions of the company to increase investor relations following a top management meeting and recent shareholder meetings concerning environmental and human ri hts policies.
-- LIB DEMS ATTACK COMPUTER 'BOMB' TIMETABLE

Liberal Democrat Treasury spokesman, Malcolm Bruce, has claimed that the government has not allocated enough money to the project to convert all civil service computer systems to cope with the date changeover imminent with the new year 2,000. The government has only pledged 7.6m stg to the scheme which a government-sponsored taskforce estimated would cost about 7bn stg.
-- BLAIR TO ISSUE PRODUCT INNOVATION CHALLENGE

With the support of the confederation of British Industry, the Royal Society of Arts and the British Council, the government Design Council has revealed its new Millennium Products Initiative to promote new products, designs and services to boost Britain's manufacturing reputation overseas. Prime minister Tony Blair revealed that the industry challenge is to be launched next month to stimulate new world-beating products from Britain for the millennium.
-- BRITISH WORKERS 'AMONG BEST OFF'

Remuneration consultants Sedgwick Noble Lowndes has released the results of a survey which shows that the average hourly take-home wage of British workers is amongst the highest for European Union countries when considerations of benefits contributions and income tax deductions are taken into consideration. The Guide to Employee Benefits and Labour Law in Europe, in which the results are published, reveals the positive effect of sterling strength on the UK's position in the earning's charts.
-- LARGE RETAILERS LIFT MARKET SHARE

Research group Corporate Intelligence on Retailing has published its annual directory, The Retail Rankings, which reveals that the UK's 10 largest retailers accounted for 36 per cent of all retail sales in 1996, up 10 per cent from the previous year. Greater market dominance is reported in the food retail sector where 63 per cent of grocery sales are taken by just four supermarket chains, Tesco , J. Sainsbury, Safeway and Asda
-- STANCHART MAY SWAP POUND FOR DOLLAR IN RESULTS

UK-based international bank Standard Chartered has announced its intention to switch accounts from pounds to dollars before the intended introduction in 1999 of the Emu single currency euro, presently being considered for use in accounts by other UK-based multinationals. The bank, which deals mostly overseas and only retains its Chartered Trust operations in the UK, sees the move as being more sensible than having to convert from dollars to pounds to euros.
-- FCM SET TO RETAIN ELECTRICITY PENSIONS BUSINESS

German Hypo-Bank controlled fund management company, Foreign & Colonial Management, is expected to retain a substantial portion of the pension schemes for the 21 electricity companies that will be reassessing their pension fund management contracts which will become free to change in April 1988. Fund management companies will be competing for the wave of pension contracts at a 'beauty parade' planned for October.
-- REED ELSEVIER SELLS TIGERPRINT

International information group Reed Elsevier has sold its greeting cards and stationary business, Tigerprint, in a 12.5m stg management- buyout deal as part of its plan for the piece-meal sale of its Reed Books division. The MBO was funded by investment capital group 3i and Allied Irish Bank and the team was lead by Peter Murphy, who has worked under Reed International Books and Marks & Spencer as well as Tigerprint.
